items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names like ConsistentHashHeader, ConsistentHashCookie and consistentHashIR say what they are, and every field has a doc comment. The only gap is small: the nested structs have no type-level docstrings (e.g. `type ConsistentHashHeader struct {` has no comment).

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The code sits in its own consistent_hash.go (363 lines) and follows the plugin pattern. But consistentHashIR keeps both the raw API slices (`headers []kgateway.ConsistentHashHeader`, cookies, ...) and the built `hashPolicies`, so the same state lives in two places. The patch is truncated, so dedup-helper reuse could not be fully checked.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Codegen added `MinLength=1` markers on the key fields, and regexutils and strconv/time are imported, which suggests regex and TTL are validated. The file body is truncated, so error propagation on bad TTL or regex values could not be confirmed. No obvious swallowed errors were visible.

items.name: Multi-policy merge semantics
items.evidence: mergeConsistentHash in merge.go is described as doing all of it: union with higher priority first, dedup, canonical re-sort, higher-priority sourceIp kept even when unset, disable honoured, and the "consistentHash" merge-origin key recorded. merge_test.go covers it and the hidden F2P tests pass.

items.name: Empty spec and disable handling
items.name_zh: 空配置与 disable 处理
items.evidence: The CEL rule `!(has(self.disable) && self.disable) || (!has(self.headers) && ...)` appears in the generated CRD YAML under x-kubernetes-validations. Tests cover the empty {} default to a single sourceIp policy and disable suppression, and the hidden tests pass.
